f124.summary: Lanssac tells Charles IX that the obstacles in Thuringia, Meissen and the Mark of Brandenburg delayed him so that he reached Poland (Mezeritz) only on 25 February, and that without the escort of the King's pensioners Alexander von Miltitz and George Luelz he would at the least have been detained; the ciphered passages hide the dangers Frenchmen met in Germany. The rest, in clear, refers to his recueil on Polish affairs.
f124.en:
Sire, ⟨since [?] the dangers which the French who pass through Germany meet with, and your ser{o r h e}⟩. The
hindrances, and the greatest causes there have been for two {?years} {...} all Thuringia, Meissen and the Mark of
Brandenburg, delayed me so much that I arrived in Poland at Mezeritz only on the twenty-fifth of February. And
without the favour I received from some of Your Majesty's servants and pensioners, principally the Sieurs Alexander
von Miltitz and George [?Luelz], who accompanied me there with a good and strong troop of their friends and assisted
me with their means, I would doubtless ⟨at the least have been detained or prevented from passing further.

f154.summary: On the eve of the Polish election, Lanssac reports to Anjou that the Lithuanian chiefs have promised their vote to him, which with the party already won should put the crown on his head, unless the Grand Seigneur's recommendation of him, made with ruse through the voivode of Wallachia, brings some unexpected change.

f156.summary: Lanssac tells Catherine that matters stand so that by next Monday she should be mother of the two greatest kings in the world, barring a change of minds, and fears that the Emperor might surprise them and that the King of Denmark, bending to his will, might give them much trouble on that side because of the strait, not half a league wide. The end of the letter (f. 157r) is in clear.

f160.summary: f. 160: the Polish nation is as venal as its German neighbours. f. 164: the Emperor has spent more than 300,000 écus in the negotiation against 30,000 on the other side and achieves nothing but to trouble Anjou's design. f. 174 (Płock, 9 May), announcing the election: it succeeded against the will of the Grand Seigneur, the Emperor, the princes of the Empire, the King of Spain, the Muscovite and the King of Sweden.

system: Homophonic letter cipher in graphic signs, two or three signs per common letter, with a dozen syllable and word signs (et, nt, st, de, ou, ns, car, pour, Allemagne, l'Empereur).
